findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is zero-argument and calls function_() instead of forwarding ...arguments_ through the limiter.
findings.impact: Any limited function that depends on its parameters receives undefined values at runtime, despite the TypeScript contract returning (...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns () => limit(() => function_()). index.d.ts:133-136 declares the returned function accepts the original Arguments tuple.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused node probe loaded index.js with an in-memory Queue stub and ran: const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); assert.equal(await limited('expected'), 'expected'); It failed with actual undefined.

findings.title: limit.map omits mapper indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The implementation conditionally passes index only when Array.isArray(iterable) is true, replacing the documented Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => ...) behavior for Set, iterator, and other iterable inputs.
findings.impact: Users mapping Set, generator, or iterator inputs receive undefined for the mapper index even though the README and type definition promise a numeric index for every iterable item.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-112 passes iterableIsArray ? index : undefined. readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 say the mapper receives item value and index for Iterable<Input>.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused node probe loaded index.js with an in-memory Queue stub and ran: const indexes = await pLimit(2).map(new Set(['a', 'b', 'c']), (_value, index) => index); assert.deepEqual(indexes, [0, 1, 2]); It failed with [undefined, undefined, undefined].

findings.title: Options object silently flips rejectOnClear default to true
findings.cause: Destructuring uses rejectOnClear = true when the concurrency argument is an object, contradicting the documented and typed default of false.
findings.impact: Calling pLimit({concurrency: 1}) now rejects queued promises on clearQueue(), so code relying on the default discard-without-reject behavior can start failing Promise.all chains with AbortError.
findings.evidence: index.js:6-8 defaults rejectOnClear to true for object options. readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document Default: false.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused node probe loaded index.js with an in-memory Queue stub, queued one running task and one pending task with pLimit({concurrency: 1}), called clearQueue(), then raced the pending promise against a short timeout. Expected pending; actual was rejected:AbortError.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: Validation checks rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean', so values like 0, null, and '' are accepted instead of rejected as non-boolean options.
findings.impact: The runtime accepts invalid JavaScript option objects that the public API and TypeScript declarations reject, making behavior depend on truthiness rather than the boolean contract.
findings.evidence: index.js:12 validates only truthy non-booleans. index.d.ts:99-106 declares rejectOnClear?: boolean, and index.test-d.ts expects rejectOnClear: 'nope' to be invalid.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused node probe loaded index.js with an in-memory Queue stub and ran: assert.throws(() => pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0}), TypeError); It failed with Missing expected exception.

findings.title: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY concurrency support was removed
findings.cause: validateConcurrency now requires Number.isInteger(concurrency), removing the explicit Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY allowance from the baseline implementation.
findings.impact: Consumers that use Infinity as an unbounded limiter now get a TypeError even though this code path previously accepted it and Infinity is a positive numeric concurrency value.
findings.evidence: git diff for index.js shows the predicate changed from (Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0 to Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0 at index.js:127-129.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused node probe loaded index.js with an in-memory Queue stub and ran: assert.doesNotThrow(() => pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)); It failed with TypeError: Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up.
